video.h

Video sessions, their pixel formats and latency, the output's dynamic metadata and its T.35 payloads, the shaders for the app's own GPU and the 3D LUT export. Includes hdrgrading.h.

The user manual's Video sessions describes the frame flow, the temporal modes and seeking in prose.

Source: include/hdrgrading/video.h

The header's own description

libhdrgrading — video: a session grades a sequence of frames (R'G'B' or planar Y'CbCr) into single-layer PQ, the scene statistics following the frames of each scene; the STATIC mapping can be written as a 3D LUT.

line 56

What a session's frames are for (hdrg_session_config_t.latency): how long a frame's output may wait and whether the session must keep up with the stream's rate (hdrg_session_output_t.late, hdrg_session_latency_report). Any preset goes with any of them.

  • PLAYBACK (default): a video being watched. The ASYNC filters keep the frames in flight they declared and the statistics look ahead (future, by default as far as they look back): delay is not limited. Late when the calls of the last second took longer a frame than the frame interval at the rate.
  • LOW (the low-latency mode: a game, a call, a live view): no frame waits for others: each job of an ASYNC filter is waited for at once, the statistics window has no future and effort AUTO is REALTIME. Late when a frame's calls took longer than the frame interval.
  • OFFLINE: converting a file nobody watches meanwhile: PLAYBACK's frames, never late, and effort AUTO is QUALITY.

The filters' time windows are the same under all of them (their algorithm reads those frames; hdrg_session_latency_report says how many), except the built-in hdrg.mctf's, which reads no frames after its own under LOW.

line 73

hdrg_session_latency_t.advice: what to change when the session is late, from what its calls took the most time with (bits):

  • PREFILTER: fewer or lighter PREFILTER filters, or their GPU versions (hdrg.metal.*, hdrg.vulkan.*, hdrg.webgpu.*)
  • EFFORT: the analysis under QUALITY: effort REALTIME
  • PROXY: the analysis: a smaller proxy (config.proxy)
  • SCALE: the SCALE stage: a smaller output or a lighter scaler
  • THREADS: the context has fewer threads than the CPUs
  • LATENCY: LOW waits for each job of an ASYNC filter: PLAYBACK keeps them in flight (frames of delay)

hdrg_session_t opaque handleline 184

typedef struct hdrg_session hdrg_session_t;

A video session: frames of one size and color in, one single-layer PQ frame out per input frame, in order. The sequence state (the color LUT, the thread pool, the apply pass's scratch) is built once. Y'CbCr frames are converted to 16-bit R'G'B' when they are sent (the ingest stage): the session holds its queue's depth + 1 of them (the most of the statistics window's future, OFFLINE's 24 frames of the lights' steadying, the SCALE stage's delay and the INTERP window's) and releases the caller's planes at once.

Temporal smoothing: a frame is analyzed when it is sent, which also tests it for a scene cut (the scene histogram and the log-average luminance against the previous frame, with no other such change in the 3 frames before: a strobe stays one scene; a fade, the log-average luminance and p99.5 moving the same way together frame after frame, is compared after moving the histogram by the change, so its steps near black do not cut it). When it is rendered, the scene anchor's statistics (p99.5 and the log-average luminance) and the APL budget's factor follow the frames of its scene:

  • WINDOWED: the log-domain mean of the anchor statistics over the scene's frames in [t - past, t + future], of the APL factor over [t - past, t].
  • RECURSIVE: an EMA in the log domain, faster toward a dimmer rendition (0.15 s) than a brighter one (0.6 s), its state in 1/1024 stop.
  • TWO_PASS: the anchor statistics are the log-domain mean over the scene's frames of the first pass (whose cuts are kept) outside its fade-outs; the APL factor is the lower of the same mean of the first pass's fits and the frame's own.
  • STATIC: no analysis and no local gain: every pixel takes the fixed mapping of its own code values (src/core/plan.h, a fixed plan), which hdrg_lut3d_export samples.

The lights' judgments follow them too, so a light judged near a threshold does not flip: under WINDOWED with a window, PLAYBACK and OFFLINE steady them place by place with the camera followed (each cell of the frame's lights takes the mean of the middle half of what the scene's frames judged where the translation of their cells that matches best from frame to frame moves it, a frame with no light there voting a boost of 0; over 8 frames before it, at most its past, and its queued future, or under OFFLINE over 24 frames before and after it, whatever the statistics' window); under LOW's WINDOWED and RECURSIVE, each light takes the median of the frame's judgment and those of the scene's frames up to 8 before it (a frame votes with its light whose center is the nearest, within 8 pixels a frame, or not at all; the lower middle of an even count: in doubt a light stays dimmer); under TWO_PASS, the median over the light's track through the scene of the first pass (a light continues the light of the frame before whose center is the nearest to its own, within 8 pixels, when its own is that light's nearest too).

The flash limiter (ITU-R BT.1702-3 Annex 1, Guideline 1; on unless flash_off, not under STATIC): the screen luminance of 16 x 9 regions is predicted from the plan's cells, and a change against the previous frame is harmful in a region when the darker side is below 160 cd/m^2 and they differ by 20 cd/m^2 or more, or above it with a Michelson contrast over 1/17. A frame whose harmful change over more than a quarter of the screen would be the seventh within a second (more than three flashes; the changes counted on the renditions before the limiter) renders with the largest gain scale below its own that keeps the change harmless against the previous frame as shown (without gain if the limiter lowered it), at the least none (the SDR rendition's change: the source's own flashes are not removed, only not amplified). Saturated red is not judged. In a fade-out under WINDOWED with a window or RECURSIVE (the log-average luminance and p99.5 falling together for three frames), the frames hold the anchor statistics and the APL factor of the frame before it (without a hold of its own), so the mapping stays and the fade stays monotonic; a fade longer than 2 seconds holds the frame 2 seconds back. From a fade's first darkening frame (TWO_PASS too, from the first pass's statistics: its scene's already stay) the lights' thresholds, the shoulder and the contrast's pivot follow the dimming against the frame before it, so the output darkens in proportion.

Seeking: a frame's output reads the frames from hdrg_session_preroll() before it to its window's future. A session created with start = n - p and preroll = p (p of at least that, or n = p) renders frame n and the frames after it byte for byte as a session started at the stream's first frame, for the same frames, pts and settings (WINDOWED, TWO_PASS, STATIC; RECURSIVE only approximately). A frame server sends frames from n - p and receives from n.

PREFILTER and SCALE filters with a time window (filter.h, filter_set_window) read the frames around their own: the session keeps them, delays each frame by the windows' future (in hdrg_session_latency) and counts their past in hdrg_session_preroll. An ASYNC filter declares in its create how many frames it keeps in flight (filter_set_max_inflight): under HDRG_LATENCY_PLAYBACK and OFFLINE they delay each frame by that less one, under HDRG_LATENCY_LOW each job is waited for at once (no delay; the GPU and the CPU take turns). hdrg_session_latency_report gives the delay by its causes, under each profile and in milliseconds. At the end of the stream the frames they hold come out with the receives.

Under WINDOWED and RECURSIVE, the first frame of a scene and every frame of a zero window render on their own statistics: they equal the still pipeline's output for the same pixels. The analysis leaves black bars at the edges (letterbox, pillarbox) out of the statistics.

The statistics across frames are a STATS filter's (the app's added to the stage, else the built-in hdrg.stats.temporal where the build has it: HDRG_WITH_TEMPORAL): without one every frame renders on its own statistics, and a window, RECURSIVE and TWO_PASS give HDRG_ERR_UNSUPPORTED (STATIC stays).

Use: send frames until HDRG_ERR_AGAIN, receive until HDRG_ERR_AGAIN, and so on; send NULL at the end, then receive until HDRG_EOF. A session is used by one thread at a time.

HDRG_API hdrg_status_t hdrg_lut3d_export(hdrg_context_t *ctx, uint8_t primaries,
                                         uint8_t transfer, const hdrg_params_t *params,
                                         const hdrg_display_caps_t *caps, uint16_t size,
                                         float *rgb);

The STATIC mapping (a session's HDRG_TEMPORAL_STATIC) as a 3D LUT, for FFmpeg lut3d, OBS or mpv: params (NULL = the defaults) on caps (NULL = hdrg_display_caps_init's), for sources of the H.273 primaries and transfer, sampled at size^3 code values (R fastest, then G, then B; node i is the 16-bit code of i / (size - 1)). rgb receives size^3 * 3 PQ R'G'B' values in [0, 1] in the rendition's container primaries, the session's 16-bit output / 65535 for those codes. size is 2..HDRG_LUT3D_MAX_SIZE. HDRG_ERR_UNSUPPORTED when filters were added to the context's SCALE or PREFILTER stage (the LUT is the color mapping alone).
